Set the constraints for the local counterfactual search

set_filters.Rd

Defines the constraints that restrict the counterfactual search in bl_find_local_cf: per-variable actionability constraints, and the switches for the feasibility (train_ranges) and plausibility (hull) rules.

Usage

set_filters(bl_target, ..., hull = TRUE, train_ranges = TRUE)

Arguments

bl_target

A "bl_target" object from bl_select_target.

...

Named per-variable constraints. Each argument name must be a variable in the model. Valid constraint values are:

"decrease"

The counterfactual value must be \(\le\) the observed value.

"increase"

The counterfactual value must be \(\ge\) the observed value.

"fixed"

The counterfactual value must be within \(\pm 0.5\) of the observed value, in model units, during the boundary search (0.5 training SD for a standardised feature). It is a tolerance, not an equality, because a point on the 2D decision boundary rarely holds a feature at exactly its observed value. After the search, bl_find_local_cf sets each fixed feature it moved back to its observed value. That point is the counterfactual if it still crosses the boundary; if it does not, no counterfactual is reported (see Fixed constraints there), so a reported counterfactual always holds a fixed feature exactly. When a sparse counterfactual is subsequently generated by bl_find_sparse_cf, any variable marked "fixed" always reverts to its observed value regardless of its Shapley classification.

c(min, max)

The counterfactual value must lie within the specified range.

"integer"

The counterfactual value must be a whole number in raw units (original units when a scaling was set via bl_set_scaling, otherwise model units), e.g. a count or a score. It combines with one of the constraints above: c("increase", "integer") (either order) for a direction or "fixed", and list(c(min, max), "integer") for a range. "integer" alone leaves the direction free. Without "integer" a feature is continuous. The search itself is continuous; bl_find_local_cf rounds the counterfactual afterwards (see Integer features there), so the Shapley values and the sparse counterfactual use whole values too. A "fixed" feature stays at its observed value and is not rounded.

hull

Logical; the plausibility rule. TRUE (the default) keeps only the boundary points inside the convex hull of the training data on each rotated plane, and drops closed boundary contours that enclose no training data there; FALSE drops the rule. Must be named. A feature called hull cannot be constrained through set_filters().

train_ranges

Logical; the feasibility rule. TRUE (the default) keeps only the boundary points whose features all lie within their training ranges (bl_result$train_ranges), and checks the restored "fixed" and rounded "integer" points against them too; FALSE drops the rule. Must be named. A feature called train_ranges cannot be constrained through set_filters().

Value

A list of class "bl_filters" with fields:

constraints

Named list of per-variable constraints.

bl_target

The "bl_target" object passed in.

hull

Logical; the plausibility switch.

train_ranges

Logical; the feasibility switch.

Actionability, feasibility and plausibility

The thesis asks a counterfactual to be actionable, feasible and plausible (defined in section 3.9.2, pp.88-90; applied in section 4.3.1, p.116):

Actionability

Each feature changes only as the person can change it: the per-variable constraints in ... (for example, age cannot decrease). None is set by default.

Feasibility

Each feature stays within the range observed in the training data (bl_result$train_ranges). Switched by train_ranges; on by default.

Plausibility

The counterfactual comes from a local decision boundary within the convex hull of the training data (p.117), so it lies in a region the training data covers: on each rotated plane, the hull of the training data, where a closed boundary contour must also enclose training data. Switched by hull; on by default.

Per-variable constraints and the training ranges are applied in X-space, after the boundary points are back-projected; the hull is applied on the rotated plane. hull = FALSE and train_ranges = FALSE with no per-variable constraint give the unconstrained counterfactual (thesis p.115): the nearest point on the model's local decision boundary, even outside the training data. Passing no filter object to bl_find_local_cf (set_filters = NULL) is the same as set_filters(bl_target): no actionability constraint, with the feasibility and plausibility rules on.
